plan: My private value is $20. In a first-round game with no history, a good strategy is to bid slightly below my true value. If others bid randomly, bidding around $15-$18 gives me a chance to win while protecting potential profit. I want to win if possible, but not overpay. Since values are randomly drawn, I expect other bidders might bid near their own values. A bid just under my value reduces risk of overpaying while still having a good winning probability.

With a private value of $29, I want to maximize potential profit. Since the prize is worth $29 to me, I'll aim to bid strategically. Given the rules of second-price auction, I want to bid close to my true value but not exactly at it. Other bidders likely have random values between $0-$49. A bid around $28-$30 seems reasonable to balance winning probability and potential profit margin.

With a private value of $45, I want to win the auction but minimize my payment. Since values are randomly drawn, other bidders might have lower or higher values. A strategic bid near my value makes sense - not exactly $45, but slightly lower to create a buffer. I'll aim to bid around $44-$44.5, which gives me a good chance of winning while preserving potential profit if my bid is slightly lower than the highest bid.
